UNLISTED DEVELOPMENT PREVIEW · SPOILERS · NO GITHUB RELEASE

THE SPARE ROOM v3.0.0 — BENEATH THE HOUSE

1. Full update overview

THE SPARE ROOM v3.0.0 — BENEATH THE HOUSE

“There was always something underneath.”

Status: unlisted, playable web development preview at /secret/. No v3.0.0 GitHub release or installers have been published. The normal website keeps its existing build. This document describes the playable scope and the direction for the major release; it is not a claim that final production QA is complete.

A permanent ten-room basement becomes the new centre of exploration. The house appears to retain domestic details its occupants cannot place. Mundane evidence suggests Dad and siblings, but signatures, dates, photographs and the sibling diary contradict one another. Mum remains the only actively present family member. Traces, voices and silhouettes never certify that a particular relative is present.

The player explores, files evidence, compares records and makes small decisions before choosing how to end the story. No countdown, holiday date or seasonal quest gates the new chapter.

Ending arithmetic: 31 established permanent endings + 30 new permanent endings = 61. The previous Halloween-era total was 44, including 13 event endings. Retiring those 13 leaves 31; this expansion adds 30, exceeding the prior total by 17 and the previous expansion size by 17. Halloween endings are absent from this preview and remain available in older builds.

Core loop: descend → explore accessible rooms → find evidence and keys → compare inconsistent records → observe quiet anomalies → make a domestic or archival decision → choose an ending, or return upstairs for supplies.

Controls retain WASD, sprint, jump, mouse capture, fullscreen, first/third-person view and close-range hold interactions. The preview has a separate story save, ending journal, camera preference and achievement store.

2. Story overview

Act I — Ordinary things: the hatch is accessible. Storage contains a familiar blanket, a coat receipt, a flat-file key and the early diary pages. The boiler branches and household boxes do not match the rooms upstairs.

Act II — A larger household: school records, photographs, drawings and worn furniture suggest more people. The family room feels cared for. The player can ask Mum about the names; she recognises small habits without endorsing a complete history.

Act III — The maintained omission: a survey route, repeated inspection dates and the hidden study suggest deliberate care for a space that is absent from some plans. The observation room raises questions about the person making the records.

Act IV — Contradictory memory: later diary entries disagree about the narrator’s relationship to the player. The player unlocks the chamber through collected evidence, not an arbitrary date or sanity threshold.

Act V — What to leave unresolved: the chamber contains an unfinished inventory and ordinary furniture. Endings concern hospitality, preservation, withdrawal, listening and uncertainty. None supplies a definitive cause or certified family tree.

Theory rules: each major family hypothesis has at least two supporting clues and one contradiction. A single anomaly is never proof. Low sanity changes how difficult exploration feels, not which account is objectively true. The category True Mystery means preserving the central question; it does not designate a canon explanation.

3. Basement design document

The hatch is in the ground-floor hallway near the fuse box. A stair interaction descends into a continuous central passage beneath the house. Five pairs of rooms open from it. The preview uses a short floor transition at the stairs; it does not claim seamless stair traversal through the existing ground-floor mesh.

| Left of passage | Right of passage |

|---|---|

| Storage Room | Boiler Room |

| Maintenance Tunnel | Archive Room |

| Forgotten Family Room | Hidden Study |

| Sealed Corridor | Observation Room |

| Former Children’s Area | Locked Chamber |

Footprint: approximately 30 × 50 metres at a floor elevation of −4 metres. The basement extends beyond the current upstairs footprint as an old service complex. Its geography is permanent and does not shuffle with the city. Door frames and colliders share the same openings. The passage is the reliable route back.

Storage Room

Purpose: Unpack a history nobody labelled.

Set dressing: Dusty shelves, folded blankets, a travel trunk and a ledger of boxes.

Contradiction: The handwriting on a recent box matches an old school label.

Progression: Inventory boxes; find the archive key.

Boiler Room

Purpose: Give the house a rhythm that is not a voice.

Set dressing: Copper pipes, pressure gauges, condensate, a service bench and an isolated valve.

Contradiction: Four branches are labelled BEDROOM. The house has fewer bedrooms.

Progression: Choose whether to stop the knocking pipe or keep its rhythm.

Maintenance Tunnel

Purpose: Follow domestic repairs into unfamiliar space.

Set dressing: Narrow service racks, cable trays, wall access panels and a measured central route.

Contradiction: A maintenance distance is longer on the return journey.

Progression: Mark a route and recover the observation key.

Archive Room

Purpose: Compare records without assuming they are reliable.

Set dressing: Flat files, labelled archive boxes, school registers and a family index.

Contradiction: Two originals carry the same document number and different household totals.

Progression: Use the storage key; compare the conflicting records; find the study key.

Forgotten Family Room

Purpose: Recognise habits before recognising faces.

Set dressing: An ordinary sofa, a low table, extra chairs, a cardigan and an unplugged radio.

Contradiction: The furniture is worn where no one is supposed to have sat.

Progression: Lay out photographs, set places and listen to the radio.

Hidden Study

Purpose: Encounter the possibility of Dad through his work.

Set dressing: Drafting tools, unfinished letters, a desk lamp and a chair facing away from the door.

Contradiction: One letter is signed Dad; another matching draft is unsigned.

Progression: Use the archive key; assemble and choose what to do with the drafts.

Sealed Corridor

Purpose: Reach an omission somebody took care to preserve.

Set dressing: Bricked door outlines, inspection tags, chalk measurements and a single accessible doorway.

Contradiction: Room numbers skip a number twice, in different places.

Progression: Isolate the noisy pipe and use the observation key.

Observation Room

Purpose: Question who was studying whom.

Set dressing: An internal window, an empty recording desk and chairs facing the family room.

Contradiction: A report describes the observer using the player’s childhood nickname.

Progression: Use the tunnel key; compare the glass, log and empty tape spool.

Former Children’s Area

Purpose: Find the traces of more than one childhood.

Set dressing: Two narrow bed frames, low hooks, a drawing wall, height marks and a toy shelf.

Contradiction: Three height columns have two dates. The pencil heights do not fit the dates.

Progression: Match drawings and height marks; discover the chamber key.

Locked Chamber

Purpose: Find a question that resists becoming an answer.

Set dressing: A plain room, two chairs, an unfinished family inventory and an unpowered door mechanism.

Contradiction: Its inventory describes furniture the player has just moved elsewhere.

Progression: Use the chamber key, twelve diary entries and three family records. Make an interpretation, not a revelation.

Key order: storage → archive key → archive → study key. The maintenance tunnel contains the observation key. The children’s area contains the chamber key. No key is stored behind the lock it opens. The sealed corridor needs the observation key and the isolated pipe. The chamber additionally needs twelve diary entries and three family records. A player can always retreat to the passage and the stairs.

4. Family mystery document

Dad: six notes and personal traces imply a parent through work, care and habits. Evidence includes a raincoat, a heating note, child-sized furniture orders and two unsigned drafts. A matching signature appears on an unrelated label. “Dad” is supported by the documents, never introduced as a confirmed new living NPC.

Siblings: the diary, two beds, school envelopes, height marks and drawings suggest one or more other children. The evidence disagrees about age, name, number and relationship. The diarist is designed as a possible sibling whose identity becomes unstable; a late page explicitly resists the player deciding too quickly.

Mum: retain her ordinary presence upstairs. New dialogue lets the player ask about the names while preserving access to the earlier family-letter interaction and established ending paths. She remembers buying a coat and making beds, but cannot attach those actions reliably to a person.

Evidence matrix:

| Hypothesis | Support | Counter-evidence |

|---|---|---|

| There were several children | Two beds; multiple school envelopes; plural drafts | Same names and registration numbers recur |

| Dad lived here | Coat receipt; workshop list; signed draft | A matching draft is unsigned; a photograph is physically inconsistent |

| Someone was deliberately omitted | Seals; cut records; room zero | Original documents also contradict the supposedly corrected copies |

| The house preserves memory | Objects recur; familiar habits outlast names | The player may contribute to what the house displays |

Do not identify a villain, diagnose the narrator, reveal a definitive family count, or use a final tape to explain everything. Let players connect the v2.7.6 missing plan, fourth place, unsigned records and maintained omission to the new evidence without turning those earlier secrets into a mandatory prerequisite.

5. The sibling diary — twenty entries

1. The long table

Mum made toast and Dad drew a boat in the butter. We argued about who got the crooked slice. I counted four cups before anyone sat down. I am writing that because I always forget ordinary things.

2. Our marks

We measured ourselves by the kitchen door. Mine is the bent line. The straight one belongs to the person who insists they are taller. Dad wrote the date twice because the first date looked wrong.

3. Saturday rain

We made a tent from two sheets. Mum said not to block the hallway. Someone kept putting a fourth cushion inside. We left it there. It made a good roof support.

4. The school photograph

Our class photographs came home. There are two envelopes with our surname and one with no name. Mum put the empty one in the drawer before I could see whether it was empty.

5. Dad’s coat

Dad let me carry his coat upstairs. It smelled of rain and the workshop. The pockets were full of small screws. One pocket had a key labelled RETURN, though I do not know what it returns.

6. The other bed

We swapped beds after the argument about the window. In the morning everybody said there had only ever been one bed. The floor is still lighter where the other feet stood.

7. The room at the end

There is a room at the end of the hall. I thought it belonged to our visitor. Nobody remembers inviting a visitor. Mum told me to leave the clean towel outside it anyway.

8. Knocking practice

Three knocks mean come in. Two mean wait. Tonight someone knocked twice from the wall beside my pillow. I waited. It seems rude to leave someone waiting, even if there is no door.

9. A quiet argument

Dad said keeping a room was not the same as keeping a person. Mum said he had agreed before. They stopped when I entered. There were four unfinished cups on the table, all still warm.

10. The spare name

My report has a name crossed out beneath mine. The teacher says she never wrote it. Her pen left the same little hook on every letter. I have copied the hook here so it cannot disappear.

11. Yesterday’s drawing

My drawing has changed. I remember giving the tall person five fingers. Now the tall person is a door, but the hand is still there. Mum says I have always drawn buildings.

12. Someone’s birthday

We lit candles without a cake. Mum said it was not a birthday. Dad could not remember why he had bought the candles. There are marks on the table from a cake tin that will not fit our cupboard.

13. The missing pronoun

I wrote WE WENT HOME. This morning it says I WENT HOME. The space is too wide for I. I keep trying to remember whose hand I was holding, and remembering a different sleeve.

14. A longer landing

It took seventeen steps to reach the bathroom. I counted twelve on the way back. Dad marked the wall with tape. In the evening the tape was wrapped around his wrist like he had always worn it.

15. The voice downstairs

Someone read my first page aloud from underneath the floor. They made the same mistake over the word crooked. I do not remember writing that mistake. I do remember being corrected.

16. Our own handwriting

There are two kinds of handwriting in this book. The second kind calls the first kind a liar. Both make the same spelling mistakes. I am leaving the mistakes where they are.

17. The person in the photograph

Dad is missing from one photograph. In the next he is holding the camera, though I can see both his hands in the picture. Mum knows which coat was his. She cannot say what he looked like.

18. A room set aside

We carried boxes to the room that is not on the plan. I remember doing it alone. My arms hurt in four places, as if someone else had been holding the same box.

19. If you find this

If you find this, do not decide too quickly who I was. I have been your sibling in some memories and your visitor in others. The room remembers a name. It will not tell me whether the name was mine.

20. An ordinary morning

Today we had toast. Someone asked for the crooked slice. There were places for everybody, which is not the same as knowing how many people there were. Please leave this page unfinished. I would like tomorrow to have somewhere to go.

6. Twenty-five new anomalies

The existing eight permanent anomalies remain above ground. These twenty-five additions occur below ground, producing 33 permanent anomaly designs overall. One new event is active at a time. Rooms select eligible unseen events before repeats. Reading and menus pause the gameplay clock; observation records a first encounter and applies any sanity cost after its panel closes. Wait and observe at a room work surface provides a deliberate discovery route.

1. The Removed Face — Forgotten Family Room

A photograph loses one silhouette, leaving a clean patch rather than a torn surface.

Presentation: A frame alternates between three and four silhouettes only after the player looks away.

Interaction: Inspect both versions; record a contradiction, not a name.

2. One More Place — Forgotten Family Room

A fourth chair appears at the table. Its legs are free of dust.

Presentation: A spare chair is enabled behind the player after a turn.

Interaction: Count the chairs and inspect the extra seat.

3. Carbon Names — Archive Room

Names emerge on a blank carbon sheet, then overlap.

Presentation: A document label reveals an additional line in oblique light.

Interaction: Read before and after switching the desk lamp.

4. Breathing Plaster — Sealed Corridor

The wall expands by a few centimetres with the boiler rhythm.

Presentation: A bounded wall inset scales slowly; collision stays fixed.

Interaction: Watch a full cycle from a safe distance.

5. The Returning Drawer — Hidden Study

A shut drawer reopens with a different small possession inside.

Presentation: A drawer slides back within its desk footprint.

Interaction: Close it twice and inspect the returned object.

6. A Second Report — Archive Room

A school report adds another pupil using the same registration number.

Presentation: A second report plane appears beside the first.

Interaction: Compare the two copies.

7. The Uncounted Minute — Boiler Room

A clock hand travels backwards while the pipe keeps time.

Presentation: Clock hands reverse; world time continues normally.

Interaction: Listen through six ticks.

8. Small Shoulders — Storage Room

A child’s coat lifts as if occupied, then hangs empty.

Presentation: A cloth-shaped rig rises and settles without approaching.

Interaction: Look away and inspect the hook.

9. The Taller Mark — Former Children’s Area

A pencil height mark rises above the adult line.

Presentation: One measured line slides upward within the board.

Interaction: Compare it with the school dates.

10. Still Warm — Forgotten Family Room

Steam rises from cups on an unpowered table.

Presentation: Three pooled translucent wisps rise over four cups.

Interaction: Inspect the unconnected kettle.

11. The Other Footfall — Maintenance Tunnel

A second footstep continues after the player stops.

Presentation: Two quiet beats and a caption trail the stopped player.

Interaction: Stand still until the extra step ends.

12. Borrowed Page — Storage Room

A diary page appears on a shelf after it was filed.

Presentation: An apparition of a collected page appears; it cannot duplicate inventory.

Interaction: Inspect the apparition to record it.

13. The Wrong Height — Former Children’s Area

The player’s shadow has a child’s proportions.

Presentation: A floor decal shortens while the camera and body stay unchanged.

Interaction: Watch the shadow without moving.

14. The Dinner Call — Forgotten Family Room

The disconnected radio counts places for dinner.

Presentation: A radio dial glows and four quiet pulses play with captions.

Interaction: Listen without turning it on.

15. The Inside Handle — Sealed Corridor

A handle turns on the bricked outline of a door.

Presentation: A brass handle rotates on a solid wall.

Interaction: Wait for it to stop; no traversable door is created.

16. The Different Initials — Storage Room

Boxes reorder their initials while the objects remain in place.

Presentation: Three labels change once when unseen.

Interaction: Read two different arrangements.

17. The Occupied Reflection — Observation Room

The glass shows occupied chairs where the real room is empty.

Presentation: Faint stationary silhouettes appear behind the pane.

Interaction: Inspect the pane and the chairs.

18. A Knock Returned — Boiler Room

The pipe repeats a rhythm with one additional beat.

Presentation: A valve wheel pulses in time with captioned tapping.

Interaction: Answer using the rhythm control.

19. Five Windows — Former Children’s Area

A drawing gains a window in a wall with no room behind it.

Presentation: A fifth cut-out window lights up on the drawing board.

Interaction: Compare the drawing with the floor plan.

20. Room Zero — Maintenance Tunnel

An inspection plate changes its room number to zero.

Presentation: A small sign flips between two numbered faces.

Interaction: Inspect the plate after the flip.

21. Someone Working — Hidden Study

The desk lamp bends toward the empty chair.

Presentation: An articulated lamp pivots slowly once.

Interaction: Stay outside the desk footprint and observe.

22. A Handprint Inside — Observation Room

A warm palm-shaped clearing appears on the far side of cold glass.

Presentation: A translucent handprint fades in behind the window.

Interaction: Inspect the far side without touching it.

23. The Long Return — Maintenance Tunnel

Perspective makes the exit seem farther away after turning.

Presentation: Non-colliding repeated arch details compress visually; real route dimensions stay fixed.

Interaction: Walk to the original survey mark.

24. Already Unpacked — Locked Chamber

An inventory lists the player’s current arrangement before it is made.

Presentation: A document lists the flags last chosen in the family room.

Interaction: Compare the list with the family table.

25. The Missing Singer — Former Children’s Area

An instrument plays a lullaby with a silent space where a voice should be.

Presentation: A toy music wheel rotates through a captioned missing verse.

Interaction: Let the entire verse finish.

Pacing: quiet captions accompany relevant sound cues, and required information is never audio-only. Events remain bounded environmental effects; they do not move a collision wall into the player or require a jumpscare. The preview uses pooled geometric representations; final art, sound mixing and animation polish remain production work.

7. Thirty new permanent endings

Every ending is a deliberate, confirmed choice at the listed room’s work surface. Meeting a condition does not end a run automatically. Existing 31 permanent paths remain accessible upstairs and in the city.

Ending 32 — Places for Everyone

Category: Family

Requirements: Family photographs · 1; Family photographs · 2; Set every suggested place in the family room. Make the final choice in the Forgotten Family Room.

Description: You set a place for every person suggested by the photographs. Mum adds one more cup, then sits down without explaining it.

Achievement: A Table Kept

Lore significance: Acknowledges possible relatives without assigning identities.

Ending 33 — The Coat at the Door

Category: Family

Requirements: Dad’s notes · 1; Family photographs · 3; Arrange the unsigned drafts in the study. Make the final choice in the Forgotten Family Room.

Description: You leave the coat where someone could collect it. In the morning it is dry. The hook is still warm.

Achievement: Expected Home

Lore significance: Dad remains an inference from belongings and drafts.

Ending 34 — Neither Bed Empty

Category: Family

Requirements: Lost drawings · 1; Lost drawings · 2; Make both beds in the children’s area. Make the final choice in the Forgotten Family Room.

Description: You make both beds. One mattress settles after the light goes out. You decide not to check which one.

Achievement: Room for Two

Lore significance: Supports a sibling reading while preserving uncertainty.

Ending 35 — The Question at Breakfast

Category: Family

Requirements: Family records · 1; Ask Mum gently about the names; Collect 6 diary entries. Make the final choice in the Forgotten Family Room.

Description: Mum listens to the names you found. She says she remembers the sound of them, but asks you not to supply the faces.

Achievement: Ask Gently

Lore significance: Mum is a witness with incomplete memories, not an exposition source.

Ending 36 — A Quiet Circuit

Category: Basement

Requirements: Dad’s notes · 2; Isolate the knocking pipe; Switch on auxiliary lighting. Make the final choice in the Boiler Room.

Description: The boiler stops knocking. Somewhere upstairs a chair is drawn back. The house has found another way to be heard.

Achievement: Circuit Open

Lore significance: Silencing one mechanism does not resolve the house.

Ending 37 — The Measured Way Out

Category: Basement

Requirements: Family records · 2; Mark the measured route. Make the final choice in the Boiler Room.

Description: You follow the marked distances to the stairs. Your final measurement leaves a person-sized space unaccounted for.

Achievement: Keep the Measure

Lore significance: Physical records can be useful and still incomplete.

Ending 38 — Maintained in Absence

Category: Basement

Requirements: Secret letters · 1; Renew the inspection seal; Isolate the knocking pipe. Make the final choice in the Boiler Room.

Description: You renew the inspection seal. By morning the signature beneath yours has been freshly added.

Achievement: Seal Renewed

Lore significance: An omitted place may still receive care.

Ending 39 — Leave the Light On

Category: Basement

Requirements: Unnumbered chamber key; Switch on auxiliary lighting; Leave the chamber door open. Make the final choice in the Boiler Room.

Description: You unlock the chamber and leave its light burning. Nobody comes out while you are watching.

Achievement: An Open Invitation

Lore significance: Offers hospitality without identifying an occupant.

Ending 40 — A Book with Both Hands

Category: Memory

Requirements: Bind both kinds of handwriting; Collect 20 diary entries. Make the final choice in the Archive Room.

Description: You bind both kinds of handwriting into one volume. The last blank page remains blank until you close the cover.

Achievement: Both Hands

Lore significance: Refuses to declare either narrator authentic.

Ending 41 — Two Originals

Category: Memory

Requirements: Keep both originals; Collect 4 family records. Make the final choice in the Archive Room.

Description: You file both originals. The drawer accepts them without resistance. For once, you do not choose which version deserves to exist.

Achievement: Keep Both Copies

Lore significance: Contradictory evidence can coexist.

Ending 42 — Names Without Faces

Category: Memory

Requirements: Family records · 3; Secret letters · 2; Copy the names without supplying faces. Make the final choice in the Archive Room.

Description: You write the names without inventing faces. At dinner Mum recognises one spelling and crosses out nothing.

Achievement: Leave the Faces Blank

Lore significance: Distinguishes preserving evidence from manufacturing certainty.

Ending 43 — The Unwritten Page

Category: Memory

Requirements: Leave the last page unfinished; Collect 12 diary entries. Make the final choice in the Archive Room.

Description: You leave a page for the person who cannot yet be described. In the quiet, a pen rolls toward it and stops.

Achievement: Leave a Margin

Lore significance: Makes room for unresolved identity.

Ending 44 — The Patient Guest

Category: Anomaly

Requirements: Set every suggested place in the family room; Observe One More Place. Make the final choice in the Observation Room.

Description: You sit beside the extra chair until morning. Its seat cools at exactly the moment yours does.

Achievement: Wait Beside It

Lore significance: An anomaly offers companionship rather than a pursuer.

Ending 45 — One Knock More

Category: Anomaly

Requirements: Return the extra beat; Observe A Knock Returned. Make the final choice in the Observation Room.

Description: You return the additional beat. The response comes from the ordinary hallway, at the height of a child’s hand.

Achievement: Return the Beat

Lore significance: Connects infrastructure to domestic memory without proving a cause.

Ending 46 — The Far Side of the Glass

Category: Anomaly

Requirements: Cover the observation pane; Observe The Occupied Reflection; Observe A Handprint Inside. Make the final choice in the Observation Room.

Description: You cover the observation pane. The covered surface reflects a room you are not standing in.

Achievement: Stop Observing

Lore significance: Questions the act of watching and recording.

Ending 47 — Walk at Their Pace

Category: Anomaly

Requirements: Mark the measured route; Observe The Other Footfall; Observe The Long Return. Make the final choice in the Observation Room.

Description: You let the second footfall set your pace. The stairs return you to an unfamiliar arrangement of familiar furniture.

Achievement: A Shared Pace

Lore significance: A path may be shared without identifying a companion.

Ending 48 — A Carefully Kept Morning

Category: Sanity

Requirements: Put the evidence down in storage; Collect 8 diary entries; Sanity at least 80%. Make the final choice in the Storage Room.

Description: You put the evidence down, eat and wait for daylight. The questions remain. You are able to ask them tomorrow.

Achievement: Return Tomorrow

Lore significance: Self-preservation is a valid ending.

Ending 49 — An Honest Uncertainty

Category: Sanity

Requirements: Keep both originals; Collect 3 family records; Sanity at least 35%; Sanity at most 65%. Make the final choice in the Storage Room.

Description: You label the file UNCONFIRMED. The letters do not rearrange themselves. That is all the reassurance you ask for.

Achievement: Unconfirmed

Lore significance: Sanity is not a truth detector.

Ending 50 — One Thing You Know

Category: Sanity

Requirements: Memory fragments · 1; Memory fragments · 2; Hold an ordinary memory; Sanity at least 1%; Sanity at most 25%. Make the final choice in the Storage Room.

Description: You hold one ordinary memory through the last of the distortion. A hand steadies yours. You do not turn to see whose.

Achievement: Hold One Memory

Lore significance: Distress never makes an interpretation definitively true.

Ending 51 — Every Page Accounted For

Category: Collector

Requirements: Collect 20 diary entries. Make the final choice in the Hidden Study.

Description: You number the twenty pages. The binding has room for twenty-one. You leave the extra space in the catalogue.

Achievement: The Unfinished Volume

Lore significance: Completeness of a collection is not completeness of history.

Ending 52 — The Household File

Category: Collector

Requirements: Collect 6 family photographs; Collect 6 family records. Make the final choice in the Hidden Study.

Description: You assemble a family file. Its contents disagree. Its cover can hold them all.

Achievement: Family Archivist

Lore significance: Records preserve a larger household, not a certified family tree.

Ending 53 — The Wall at Their Height

Category: Collector

Requirements: Make both beds in the children’s area; Collect 5 lost drawings. Make the final choice in the Hidden Study.

Description: You hang every drawing at the height of its maker. One hangs above the height marks; another below the skirting.

Achievement: At Their Height

Lore significance: The children cannot be arranged into a reliable chronology.

Ending 54 — Nothing Discarded

Category: Collector

Requirements: Collect 4 secret letters; Collect 8 memory fragments. Make the final choice in the Hidden Study.

Description: You take every fragment to the stairs. Upstairs, a box waits with your handwriting and no date.

Achievement: Nothing Discarded

Lore significance: Collection leads to another possible history, not a final solution.

Ending 55 — The Room Number Nobody Used

Category: Secret

Requirements: Family records · 4; Inspection-window key; Record room zero; Observe Room Zero. Make the final choice in the Sealed Corridor.

Description: You enter zero in the inventory. A door clicks shut elsewhere. The corridor still contains the same number of openings.

Achievement: Room Zero

Lore significance: An absent number may refer to a person, a space or an accounting error.

Ending 56 — An Unsigned Father

Category: Secret

Requirements: Arrange the unsigned drafts in the study; Collect 6 Dad’s notes. Make the final choice in the Sealed Corridor.

Description: You leave the final letter unsigned. Mum calls it his handwriting, then asks whose desk you found it in.

Achievement: Unsigned

Lore significance: Keeps the father hypothesis unsettled.

Ending 57 — Candles Without a Cake

Category: Secret

Requirements: Someone’s birthday; Family photographs · 4; Lost drawings · 3; Light the unclaimed candles. Make the final choice in the Sealed Corridor.

Description: You light the unclaimed candles. Wax falls in four separate pools. Nobody says a birthday wish aloud.

Achievement: An Unclaimed Birthday

Lore significance: A shared ritual outlasts its explanation.

Ending 58 — A Place in the Wall

Category: Secret

Requirements: Secret letters · 3; Listen without naming the sound; Observe 10 distinct new anomalies. Make the final choice in the Sealed Corridor.

Description: You spend a night listening to the wall. In the morning a recording contains only your own careful breathing.

Achievement: Listen Without Naming

Lore significance: Questions whether the listener contributes to the haunting.

Ending 59 — The Inventory Remains Open

Category: True Mystery

Requirements: Keep both originals; Leave the chamber door open; Collect 20 diary entries; Collect 6 family records. Make the final choice in the Locked Chamber.

Description: You leave the household inventory open. One column is headed PRESENT. The other has no heading. Neither column stays empty.

Achievement: An Open Inventory

Lore significance: The central family question remains deliberately unanswered.

Ending 60 — Do Not Correct the House

Category: True Mystery

Requirements: Leave the last page unfinished; Mark the measured route; Observe 25 distinct new anomalies. Make the final choice in the Locked Chamber.

Description: You preserve every version of the plan. The house is quieter when it is no longer being asked to agree with you.

Achievement: No Correction Necessary

Lore significance: Observation changes the relationship, not the certainty of the lore.

Ending 61 — Somewhere for Tomorrow

Category: True Mystery

Requirements: Ask Mum gently about the names; Bind both kinds of handwriting; Leave the last page unfinished; Collect 20 diary entries; Collect 8 memory fragments. Make the final choice in the Locked Chamber.

Description: You leave the last page unfinished. At breakfast Mum asks whether you slept well. For once you tell her about a dream instead of supplying an answer.

Achievement: Somewhere for Tomorrow

Lore significance: Begins a new era while leaving the family mystery open.

9. Collectible designs

59 permanent collectible objects: 20 diary entries, 6 Dad’s notes, 6 photographs, 5 drawings, 6 family records, 4 secret letters, 8 memory fragments and 4 keys. Paper evidence lies on inspected work surfaces; room stations support comparisons and decisions. Every object has a readable panel and notebook transcription. Rereading costs no sanity. Nothing essential requires reading tiny world text.

First-discovery sanity costs: early paper evidence 1%, later diary entries 3%, memory fragments 4%; keys cost none. Existing difficulty scaling remains in effect. These losses queue until the reading panel closes. Existing kitchen food recovery remains available upstairs.

10. Technical improvements and verification

Preview implementation:

  • Exact segment/box occlusion for interaction targets and text overlays; opaque floors participate at negative as well as positive elevations.
  • Geometry is batched by room and material. Floor-aware culling hides the surface when below ground and the basement when upstairs.
  • Room visibility uses the passage, physical door openings and line-of-sight checks. Depth testing remains authoritative for individual objects.
  • The compatibility renderer filters room/floor geometry too.
  • Room-specific interaction candidates prevent selection on the other floor; hold progress cancels on range, visibility, target or menu changes.
  • Basement walls, locked door panels and aligned frames share their gameplay geometry. Movement is sampled against thin obstacles.
  • One active new anomaly and reusable scene groups bound allocation. Three local basement lights are reused rather than adding a light per room.
  • Save validation handles the new optional schema; last-known-good backup recovery remains in place. Story, ending journal, camera and achievements use dedicated v3 keys.
  • Geometry-versioned visibility indexing and cached text textures reduce repeated work. Startup texture work retains the v2.7.6 reduction.
  • No seasonal scripts, countdowns or retired Halloween ending actions load at /secret/.

Release gates before a public v3 release: measure startup and frame times on representative hardware; verify actual WebGL on supported browsers and desktop builds; exercise old saves and corrupt/interrupted writes; complete each key route without map travel or admin; inspect stair transitions, third-person occlusion and note visibility from both floors; confirm all 61 permanent endings, 40 new achievements and retired-event isolation. Final art and audio polish, device coverage and performance benchmarking are not claimed complete by this development preview.

11. Marketing description

THE SPARE ROOM v3.0.0 — BENEATH THE HOUSE

There was always something underneath.

Halloween has gone. The hallway is quiet again.

The maintenance hatch is open.

Below the family house are boxes nobody remembers packing, beds nobody remembers making, and twenty diary pages written by someone who may have shared your childhood.

A coat suggests a father. A school report suggests another child. The next document disagrees.

Explore ten permanent basement areas, collect a larger household’s forgotten belongings and discover thirty new permanent endings. Twenty-five quiet anomalies turn familiar domestic details into questions you cannot put back in their boxes.

The house remembers more people than Mum can name.

Why?

An unlisted development preview is playable at /secret/. A public release date has not been announced.

12. Complete GitHub release notes — draft only

THE SPARE ROOM v3.0.0 — BENEATH THE HOUSE

“There was always something underneath.”

DRAFT RELEASE NOTES — NOT PUBLISHED TO GITHUB

This is the planned release wording for the unlisted development preview. Publish it only after production verification is complete.

A permanent new chapter

  • Added a ten-area basement: Storage Room, Boiler Room, Maintenance Tunnel, Archive Room, Forgotten Family Room, Hidden Study, Sealed Corridor, Observation Room, Former Children’s Area and Locked Chamber.
  • Added evidence suggesting Dad, siblings and a larger household. Contradictory records leave their history unresolved.
  • Added twenty collectible sibling-diary entries and a readable family notebook.
  • Added 59 collectible objects across eight evidence types, including four progression keys.
  • Added twenty-five environmental anomalies with quiet, room-aware pacing.
  • Added thirty permanent endings across Family, Basement, Memory, Anomaly, Sanity, Collector, Secret and True Mystery categories.
  • Added forty achievements: thirty for new endings and ten for exploration.

The end of the Halloween era

The thirteen Halloween event ending paths are retired from v3.0.0. Earlier builds retain their event content and journals. The established 31 permanent endings remain, joined by 30 new paths: **61 permanent endings**, exceeding the prior 44-path Halloween-era total.

Visibility and stability

  • Fixed sticky notes and wall-attached evidence appearing through floors or from upstairs viewing angles.
  • Added room-based visibility checks and floor-based rendering culling.
  • Improved occlusion and object visibility management.
  • Improved basement collision and aligned doorway geometry.
  • Bounded anomaly allocation with reusable visuals and local lighting.
  • Improved save validation, backup recovery and preview-save isolation.
  • Reduced repeated visibility and texture work. Loading and frame-time improvements require final hardware benchmarking before quantified claims are published.
  • General bug fixes and stability improvements.

Playing the preview

The unlisted web preview is at /secret/. It uses a separate save slot. It is not a password-protected private build. The normal website remains on its existing version.

WASD walk · Shift sprint · Space jump · V first/third person. Move close to a visible object and hold E or hold click. Read collected evidence again in FAMILY NOTEBOOK. Kitchen sandwiches restore sanity according to the selected difficulty.

New disturbing discoveries apply sanity loss after the reading panel closes. Menus pause gameplay timers. No calendar gate locks the basement.

Development status

This preview is not a GitHub release. No v3.0.0 installers have been published. Final art/audio polish, cross-platform installer QA and performance benchmarking remain required before release. Please report your browser, mode, location, generation code and what happened. Mark family evidence and endings as spoilers.

The house has kept a place for someone.
